subject: Bizarre bug in interaction of facet_wrap and geom_abline

messages.author: d2ca95393bc23535
messages.subject: Bizarre bug in interaction of facet_wrap and geom_abline
parts:
Dea Ggplotters,
Thanks again for all you do to make this fantastic package for the community.

I found an odd bug/interaction between facet_wrap and geom_abline, that only happens if the data argument is omitted from the main ggplot call before faceting. Although there's an easy workaround, it seems like this shouldn't happen. Code example below; I used ggplot2 v1.0.

# this works
ggplot() +
    geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
    facet_wrap(~color)

# this also works
ggplot() +
    geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
    geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) 

# this doesn't work, returning a cryptic error "Error in if (empty(data)) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"
ggplot() +
    geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
    geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
    facet_wrap(~color)

# however, this works, just moving the "data" to the ggplot call from geom_point
ggplot(data=diamonds) +
    geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
    geom_point(aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
    facet_wrap(~color)


Best wishes,
Edward

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Bizarre bug in interaction of facet_wrap and geom_abline
parts:
Hi:

This is not a bug; it has to do with the training process that takes
place when ggplot2 generates a plot (Figure 3.7, p. 36 of the ggplot2
book).

On Mon, Feb 2, 2015 at 1:55 PM, Edward Wallace <ewjwa...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Dea Ggplotters,
> Thanks again for all you do to make this fantastic package for the
> community.
>
> I found an odd bug/interaction between facet_wrap and geom_abline, that only
> happens if the data argument is omitted from the main ggplot call before
> faceting. Although there's an easy workaround, it seems like this shouldn't
> happen. Code example below; I used ggplot2 v1.0.
>

This chunk works because there is one layer and the data frame is
defined in the call that generates it.

> # this works
> ggplot() +
> geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
> facet_wrap(~color)
>

This works because there is only one plot region and the data frame is
defined in one of the two layers. The other (geom_abline()) 'inherits'
the data frame from geom_point() by default.

> # this also works
> ggplot() +
> geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
> geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price))
>


> # this doesn't work, returning a cryptic error "Error in if (empty(data)) {
> : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"

It doesn't work because when faceting, ggplot2 needs to know which
data frame is to be used in each layer. You defined a data frame for
geom_point() but not for geom_abline(), so as far as the system is
concerned, you've specified an empty data frame for geom_abline().
This is because of the presence of facet_wrap(), which is dealt with
very early in the plot generation process (step 2, after the mapping
of variables to aesthetics).

If you define data = diamonds in geom_abline(), it works. This is
typically what you need to do if you do not specify a 'primary' data
frame in the base layer defined by ggplot().

> ggplot() +
> geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
> geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
> facet_wrap(~color)
>

This is the usual behavior, which one would expect since one data
frame is being used for all layers.

> # however, this works, just moving the "data" to the ggplot call from
> geom_point
> ggplot(data=diamonds) +
> geom_abline(slope=10000,intercept=0) +
> geom_point(aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
> facet_wrap(~color)
>

The typical situations in which an empty ggplot() base layer is
appropriate are those for which different sets of aesthetics are used
in different layers and/or different data frames are used across
several layers (e.g., if you use different data sets for geom_point()
and geom_text(), with different variables mapped to x and y in each) .
For the problem you posed, I would have used

ggplot(data = diamonds, aes(x = carat, y = price)) +
geom_point() +
geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1e4) +
facet_wrap(~ color)

The reason I would populate the argument list of ggplot() this way is
because the diamonds data set is used in each layer, as are the carat
and price variables.

Dennis

>
> Best wishes,
> Edward

messages.author: d2ca95393bc23535
messages.subject: Re: Bizarre bug in interaction of facet_wrap and geom_abline
parts:
Hi Dennis,
Thanks for the reply. I guess here I'm using geom_abline like an annotation, although:
# this does not work either in that it doesn't draw a line
ggplot() +
    annotate(geom="abline",slope=10000,intercept=0) +
    geom_point(data=diamonds,aes(x=carat,y=price)) +
    facet_wrap(~color)

Even though you've made clear it's a design decision, I'm struggling to understand the rationale, and personally am confused by the lack of consistency with/without faceting - if the lack of data frame is not a problem with fixed values on one panel, why not on many panels? Goodness knows I'm not a software architect, however.

Best wishes,
Edward
